key_insight: ShapeR can synthesize complete, high-quality 3D object shapes from casual, noisy image sequences by fusing sparse SLAM cues, 3D detections, and vision–language priors to condition a robust generative shape model.
problem_solved: Most conditional 3D generation methods require clean, segmented, unoccluded inputs; ShapeR enables reliable 3D shape generation from real-world, casually captured video where observations are sparse, occluded, and noisy.
method: Extract sparse 3D structure and camera poses from casual captures using off‑the‑shelf visual–inertial SLAM.
Associate and enrich object observations with 3D detection/segmentation and vision–language models to provide semantic and instance-level cues.
Condition a robust generative 3D shape model on the fused sparse spatial cues + semantic priors, with training and fusion strategies that tolerate occlusion and noise.
impact: Makes practical 3D shape reconstruction feasible from everyday captures (phones, handheld rigs) without controlled scanning—accelerating dataset creation, AR/VR content generation, and perception for robotics and vision systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: casual video → SLAM map & poses → 3D detection + VLM cueing → conditioned generative model → full 3D shape

paper_title: ShapeR: Robust Conditional 3D Shape Generation from Casual Captures
